office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: House Majority Floor Leader Monica Stonier, who has held this Vancouver seat since 2016, faces Republican Derek Thompson, a retired cosmetology instructor who lost a 2025 Vancouver City Council race. Stonier runs on a long voting and sponsorship record; Thompson's brief platform centers on the school funding formula, avoiding unnecessary taxes and efficient spending.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and House Majority Floor Leader, an Evergreen Public Schools access coach and former middle-school teacher, seeking re-election on childcare, housing, special-education funding and healthcare costs.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and defended it at an April town hall [S5][S4]
Voted for the 2025 capital gains, excise and B&O tax increases [S6][S7][S8]
Prime sponsor of the 2025 law that rewrote the Initiative 2081 parents' rights, removing some notification rights [S10]
Voted for the 2025 limits on residential rent increases [S9]
Voted for the 2023 reproductive and gender-affirming care protections [S14][S15]

taxes.basis: Yea on ESSB 6346 (2026) and on the 2025 capital gains, excise and B&O tax increases; defended the income tax at a town hall.

spending.basis: Calls for real funding for special education, childcare and housing and describes the operating budget as a contract with the people.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217's limits on rent and fee increases; cites Clark County's eviction rate.

social.basis: Voted for ESHB 1469 (reproductive and gender-affirming care shield law) and ESSB 5599 (youth seeking protected health care).

parental-rights.basis: Prime sponsor of ESHB 1296, which eliminated several Initiative 2081 parental notification rights and lengthened records access to 45 days; also voted for ESSB 5181.

experience.basis: In the House since 2016 after earlier serving the 17th District; House Majority Floor Leader.

immigration.basis: Cites new protections for immigrant workers among her work; pamphlet says she stands with neighbors under federal attack.

healthcare.basis: Healthcare agenda works within the current system: required insurance coverage of infertility treatment (HB 1730) and capital funding for dental access.

candidates.summary: Retired cosmetology instructor and former Nike department supervisor, a first-time legislative candidate who lost a 2025 Vancouver City Council race, running on school funding, cost of living and efficient use of tax dollars.
highlights: Pledges to "fix school funding at the source" [S1]
Says fiscal accountability starts with protecting families from "unnecessary taxes" [S2]
Says education funding should focus on classrooms, "not bureaucracy" [S2]
Would protect legacy businesses from being sidelined by major infrastructure projects [S1]

taxes.basis: Campaign plank on protecting families from unnecessary taxes; no statement on the 2026 income tax.

spending.basis: Pledges efficient use of tax dollars and classroom spending over bureaucracy.

experience.basis: No elected experience; says he is not a career politician; lost his only prior race (2025 Vancouver council).
